title: Man killed by police had been charged with theft, court records show
article: A Kamloops man killed by police Monday was to have appeared in court today on a theft charge.
Court records showed Tuesday that Stephen Mace Hanaghan, 45, was charged June 16 with theft under $5,000. Records show he faced a similar charge for a theft that occurred during the summer of 2003.
Hanaghan was shot and killed moments after he backed a 1984 red and white Chevy into an RCMP Suburban on Noble Lake Road early Monday morning.
Kamloops RCMP Cpl. Fran Bethell confirmed the pickup had been stolen from outside a Kamloops business. She did not know which business. The theft had not been reported to police.
Hanaghan and his 45-year-old male passenger were pursued through Westsyde by police after witnesses spotted them breaking into the Super Save gas station on Westsyde Road, she said.
Speeds during the chase reached as high as 110-120 km/h before the pickup turned on to the winding gravel forestry road and into a cutting block.

The pursuit continued for seven kilometres before Hanaghan reportedly stopped the vehicle and backed it into the Suburban. At that point the officer, a nine-year police veteran, fired his handgun several times at Hanaghan, killing him.
The passenger was arrested at the scene. He was released Monday night without charges, Bethell said.
"The investigation into the attempted break and enter at the gas station is also still ongoing. Charges specifically related to the break and enter are anticipated," she said.

B.C. regional coroner Jeff Dolan said an autopsy is expected to be performed on Hanaghan sometime today. He said more information, including how many times Hanaghan was shot, could be released after it is completed.
Bethell said five officers from the Kelowna RCMP major crimes unit have taken over the investigation. An independent commissioned officer who will oversee the investigation has yet to be assigned.
